How to handle a customer complaint at the service desk.

Start by listening without interrupting. Let the customer finish explaining even if you already know the answer, because people calm down faster once they feel heard.

Next, repeat the problem back in your own words and confirm that you've understood it correctly. If the issue involves a repair that went wrong, pull up the work order and check the technician's notes before you respond.

You can authorise a credit of up to $100 without approval. Anything above that goes to the service manager, and you should write down the customer's name and phone number so we can call them back within 24 hours.

Case study draft, the garden centre relaunch.

Background, a regional garden centre chain with 14 locations came to us in January because sales had been flat for two years and their website was hard to use on phones. They had no consistent visual identity, so every store looked slightly different.

What we did, we rebuilt the website from scratch, designed a new logo and signage system, and ran a six-week social campaign focused on locally grown plants. Antonio led the photography and the results speak for themselves.

Results, online orders rose by 140% within four months, and average basket size increased from $11 to $15.

Feature request, bulk edit for opportunities. Right now sales reps have to open each opportunity one by one to change the stage or the close date, which is painful when we're cleaning up the pipeline at the end of the quarter. What we'd like is a checkbox on each row in the list view and a bulk actions menu at the top. The menu should let you change the stage, reassign the owner and update the close date for all selected rows at once. It would also be good to show a confirmation dialogue that lists how many records will change. As a nice-to-have, an undo option for 30 seconds after the change would save us a lot of headaches. Tarek from the ops team estimates this would save each rep about three hours a week.
